<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Delivers PRD 001 rows req-02, req-03 and req-04, and starts req-05, req-17 and req-19. Builds blueprint components c-role-schema, c-layout and c-writer. Sources: docs/project/prds/001-pij-community.dd.json, docs/project/blueprints/001-pij-community.dd.json, docs/project/roadmaps/001-pij-community.dd.json (s02), docs/project/workshops/001-pij-community/001-community-directory.md. The hand-written directory it will later import is <government-root>/community/ on the prime-governance branch (README there). Store migration number 0031 is claimed for this plan by pm-001.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A role definition, an output and a memory note each have a ddocs schema that accepts the PRD's fields and refuses a role without scope or a standing packet.
- `pij directory add <id>` writes a validated role under <government-root>/community/roles/<id>/ and commits it on the governance branch, attributed to the calling seat.
- A directory write never stages, overwrites or reverts anyone's uncommitted work, including the prime's governance checkout.
- Missing governance and missing ddocs each refuse by name with a runnable next step.
- A write costs a handful of launches per request, never per tick or per seat, and the cost is measured.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Assign, release, lineage and the `pij directory` view (s04).
- Role templates and core roles on directory creation (s03).
- The routing table (s08), send to a role (s05), the `pij output` verb and notification (s06), memory prompts (s07), number claims (s11).
- Importing the live hand-written directory. The prime runs that with the batch mode after deploy.
- Pushing the governance branch. pij commits; it never pushes.

If any path the writer is about to write already carries an edit it did not make (modified, staged or untracked), it refuses by name and writes nothing. <a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Findings from planning, 2026-11-04. (1) Rust has no governance-root resolver yet; only harness/scripts/government-root.sh, which finds the one worktree with prime-governance checked out. (2) ddocs finds schemas at <gitroot>/.dd, then .harness/.dd, then ~/.dd. The governance branch is an orphan with no .dd/, so pij/role documents there cannot validate until schemas are reachable from it (open question 3). (3) ddocs is not a repo dependency: no node_modules/.bin/ddocs in pij; the global `ddocs` links to a local checkout at ~/substrate/dd. CI will not have it. (4) The daemon already launches git through pij_core::program::launch and records sites with pij_core::spawns::record (crates/daemon/src/orchestration/repo.rs, http/governance.rs, pa_watchdog.rs); spawn_sites.rs fails on bare `git` launches. (5) The prime's governance worktree has prime-governance checked out. Moving that branch's tip from outside leaves the checkout's index behind, so its next commit would record pij's files as deleted (open question 2).

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The prime's governance checkout goes stale when pij moves the branch tip, and its next commit silently reverts pij's write. | High | Critical | Ruling C8: commit only the writer's own paths with `git commit --only` in the governance worktree, refuse on foreign edits to them; AC4 proves it. |
| ddocs is absent in CI and on other machines. | High | Medium | Ruling C10: injected fake for unit tests; named refusal and doctor check at runtime. |
| Schemas on main and on the governance branch drift apart. | Medium | Medium | Ruling C9: the writer refreshes the copies when pij's schema version moves. |
| macOS /usr/bin/git is an xcrun shim that starts extra processes. | Medium | Low | Use pij_core::program::launch as the existing git sites do; count real launches in the cost row. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Never write to the live governance branch or the prod daemon; scratch repos and a private daemon only.
- Builds scoped with -p. Check `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` before a large build; stop and tell pm-001 under 25 GB.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, never push refs/notes/*.
- Phase 2 may start before phase 1 lands, but nothing that parses a role, output or memory document is merged as done until phase 1's schemas are merged in and AC1's fixtures pass through the writer.
